clinical.citation: Macrocephaly and developmental delay caused by missense variants in RAB5C (PMID: 37552066)

variants.description: 9 different heterozygous de novo missense variants (specific variants not individually listed in abstract)
2 loss of function variants (specific variants not individually listed in abstract)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: de novo variants, in vitro biochemical studies showed all four tested missense variants were damaging with increased nucleotide exchange rate and attenuated responsivity to guanine exchange factors, C. elegans and zebrafish models confirmed in vivo pathogenicity, dominant negative mechanism demonstrated for two variants

clinical.citation: A de novo 17q21.2 duplication in a boy with developmental delay and dysmorphic features (PMID: 23337768)

variants.description: de novo 103 kb duplication at 17q21.2 including RAB5C and 7 other genes

clinical.diagnostic_reason: de novo duplication not previously reported, array-CGH confirmed, RAB5C included among 8 genes in duplicated region; however, three other genes (KAT2A, KCNH4, STAT5B) also implicated in intellectual deficiency

model_organism.citation: Rab5c-mediated endocytic trafficking regulates hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell development via Notch and AKT signaling (PMID: 32275659)
phenotypes: Defects in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) production
Reduced survival of HE in ventral wall of dorsal aorta
Excessive endolysosomal trafficking upon Rab5c overactivation leading to HSPC production defects

model_organism.citation: Wnt11 functions in gastrulation by controlling cell cohesion through Rab5c and E-cadherin (PMID: 16198297)
phenotypes: Phenotype mimics slb/wnt11 mutants when Rab5c activity is blocked
Rescue of slb/wnt11 mutant phenotype when Rab5c activity is enhanced

model_organism.citation: Establishment and analysis of conditional Rab1- and Rab5-knockout cells using the auxin-inducible degron system (PMID: 34817057)
phenotypes: Cell death 48 hours after Rab5 protein depletion
Dramatic reduction in intracellular signals of endocytic cargos via receptor-mediated endocytosis
Dramatic reduction in intracellular signals of endocytic cargos via fluid-phase endocytosis

model_organism.citation: The endosomal RIN2/Rab5C machinery prevents VEGFR2 degradation to control gene expression and tip cell identity during angiogenesis (PMID: 33983539)
phenotypes: Disrupted VEGF signaling through ERK and PI3-K pathways
Reduced expression of immediate VEGF target genes
Defects in specification of angiogenic tip and stalk cell phenotypes
Defects in developmental angiogenesis in vivo
Defects in tip cell formation and migration

model_organism.citation: Prolonged visual experience accelerates developmental synaptic downscaling via epigenetic regulation and Rab5c mediated AMPA receptor trafficking (PMID: 41507541)
phenotypes: Accelerated developmental decline of glutamatergic synaptic transmission
Reduced miniature excitatory postsynaptic current (mEPSC) amplitudes
Rab5c-dependent endocytosis of AMPA receptor subunits GluA1 and GluA2
Reversible synaptic transmission and AMPAR expression upon re-exposure to standard light conditions

biological.citation: S100P is a ferroptosis suppressor to facilitate hepatocellular carcinoma development by rewiring lipid metabolism (PMID: 39779666)
biological.summary: RAB5C directs acetyl-CoA carboxylase alpha (ACC1) to lysosomes via P62-dependent selective autophagy in hepatocellular carcinoma cells. Knockdown of RAB5C abrogates S100P-induced lysosomal degradation of ACC1 and restores ferroptosis resistance in HCC cells.

biological.citation: Macrocephaly and developmental delay caused by missense variants in RAB5C (PMID: 37552066)
biological.summary: RAB5C missense variants were investigated in C. elegans and zebrafish embryos, showing defects in endocytic pathway function. All four tested variants were damaging in vivo, with some exhibiting dominant negative mechanisms and resulting in defective development in zebrafish.
biological.sample_size: 12 individuals with 9 different RAB5C variants; 4 variants experimentally investigated

biological.citation: Organelle-selective click labeling coupled with flow cytometry allows pooled CRISPR screening of genes involved in phosphatidylcholine metabolism (PMID: 36917984)
biological.summary: RAB5C was identified in a genome-scale CRISPR-knockout screen as a gene involved in vesicular membrane trafficking and phosphatidylcholine metabolism. RAB5C knockdown altered organellar phosphatidylcholine phenotypes detectable by flow cytometry.

biological.citation: RAB5C, SYNJ1, and RNF19B promote male ankylosing spondylitis by regulating immune cell infiltration (PMID: 34277811)
biological.summary: RAB5C was identified as a key differentially expressed gene in male ankylosing spondylitis patients through integrated PPI network and WGCNA analysis. RAB5C expression correlates with increased monocyte and macrophage infiltration, suggesting a role in immune cell regulation in AS pathogenesis.
biological.sample_size: Male AS patients and male healthy controls (specific n not stated)

biological.citation: Effects of miR-145 targeting rab5c and regulating MAPK/ERK signaling pathway on proliferation and invasion of thyroid papillary carcinoma cells (PMID: 37213158)
biological.summary: miR-145 directly targets RAB5C mRNA (confirmed by luciferase reporter assay), and miR-145 overexpression or RAB5C knockdown inhibits thyroid papillary carcinoma cell proliferation and invasion while activating MAPK/ERK signaling in TPC-1 cells.

biological.citation: RAB5C, a new mRNA binding target of HuR, regulates breast cancer cell proliferation (PMID: 36480789)
biological.summary: HuR RNA-binding protein directly binds to RAB5C mRNA 3'UTR and stabilizes RAB5C transcript, promoting breast cancer cell proliferation. RAB5C suppression reduces BC cell growth, indicating RAB5C functions as an oncogene in breast cancer.
biological.sample_size: BC tissues and MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 cell lines

biological.citation: Rab5c promotes RSV and ADV replication by autophagy in respiratory epithelial cells (PMID: 38242290)
biological.summary: RAB5c promotes respiratory syncytial virus and adenovirus replication through autophagy, not endocytosis, by interacting with Beclin1 to upregulate LC3-II expression in A549 cells and in RAB5c-overexpressing mice. Activated RAB5c promotes viral replication while inactivated RAB5c inhibits it.

biological.citation: RAB5C Increases Endothelial Release of VWF by Regulating Vesicle Trafficking (PMID: 41537263)
biological.summary: Two genetic variants (rs9915255 and rs9912088) identified by GWAS for von Willebrand Factor levels regulate RAB5C expression in endothelial cells. RAB5C regulates VWF exocytosis through interaction with SNAP29, a SNARE protein controlling vesicle fusion, with constitutively active RAB5C increasing VWF release.

biological.citation: RAB5c controls the assembly of non-canonical autophagy machinery to promote phagosome maturation and microbicidal function of macrophages (PMID: 40196584)
biological.summary: RAB5c is necessary for LC3-associated phagocytosis (LAP) and regulates phagosome recruitment of complexes required for PI(3)P and ROS generation. RAB5c facilitates V-ATPase translocation to phagosomes for ATG16L1 binding and LC3 conjugation, with RAB5c depletion impairing macrophage elimination of Aspergillus fumigatus.

biological.citation: Rab5C enhances resistance to ionizing radiation in rectal cancer (PMID: 30968159)
biological.summary: RAB5C is overexpressed in radiotherapy-resistant rectal adenocarcinoma cells and tissues. RAB5C modulates EGFR internalization and nuclear relocalization in response to irradiation, affecting expression of DNA repair proteins Ku70 and Ku80, thereby promoting radiotherapy resistance.
biological.sample_size: Stage II and III rectal adenocarcinoma patients

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - Coronary artery disease-associated splicing variants in vascular smooth muscle cells (PMID: N/A)
biological.summary: RAB5C was identified as one of six genes with colocalized genetic signals between splice effect associations (sQTLs) and CAD risk in vascular smooth muscle cells. CAD-associated SNPs in RAB5C are predicted to affect smooth muscle cell-specific alternative splicing events.
biological.sample_size: 151 heart transplant donors; 6 aortic SMC donors for long-read sequencing
